text:
maria: seeing weird KV memory growth on Mistral-7B when serving very long conversations (~60k tokens). RSS increments ~1.8-2.2GB per 10k tokens on repeated prompts, even after supposed eviction. Not reproducible on Llama runs.
aj: hmm that sounds like a KV residency leak or fragmentation. which kernel combo are you using? gqa/mqa? quant?

maria: serving with MQA path (fp16 + custom q4/ggml-ish kernels), kernel selection falls back to 'mistral_mqa_kernel_v3' for longseq. We also have rope scaling enabled.

kai: can you paste the allocator stats from the runtime (kv/journal pages)? short snippet is fine.

maria: pasted quick dump: ```
KV_PAGES_TOTAL=43812
KV_PAGES_FREE=3124
KV_PAGE_CHUNKS=1976
KV_FRAGMENTATION_RATIO=0.28
RECENT_EVICTED=0
EVICT_SCAN_CYCLES=0
```

maria: also attaching a short log line of repeated requests: ```
[2026-03-15T14:02:03Z] req id=abc token_count=10240 kv_alloc=+2048MB RSS=36.1GB
[2026-03-15T14:02:07Z] req id=def token_count=20480 kv_alloc=+1800MB RSS=37.9GB
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] req id=ghi token_count=30720 kv_alloc=+2100MB RSS=39.7GB
```

sam: interesting that RECENT_EVICTED is 0. Are we skipping eviction under certain rope-scaling thresholds? Could be a policy bug where long-prefix caching disables sweep.
aj: do we have a repro script? maybe we can run with timeline sampling and heap profiles. also try forcing kernel switch to the Mistral small-kernel path to see if it's kernel-specific.

maria: repro is here: https://intra/runs/kv-longseq-repro-4415 (internal) — but quick local steps: run batch of 50 requests with incremental prefixes to 60k tokens, model=Mistral-7B-mqa, rope_scale=1.0.

perf-bot: new flamegraph uploaded: https://perfdash/flame/4415012345 (shows heavy time in kv_rebuild and slab_coalesce).

kai: flamegraph note: a lot of time in kv_rebuild -> page_walk -> kernel_prefetch. Suggests kernel triggers page pinning and prevents sweep.
irene: on Qwen we saw similar but it was caused by MQA->GQA fallback not clearing slot metadata. Could be cross-model bug where fallback path leaves stale references.
aj: two hypotheses: 1) kernel-specific pinning prevents eviction during long sequences, 2) rope scaling interaction changes residency heuristics so pages never qualify for eviction. Both could lead to fragmentation + apparent leak.

sam: quick experiment idea: toggle `kv_evict_threshold` to 0.5 and run a short replay. If RSS stabilizes, it's eviction policy; if not, it's kernel pinning.

maria: ran toggle locally: with threshold 0.5 RSS still increases but slower (~0.9GB per 10k). With forced kernel 'mistral_small_kernel' RSS stabilizes after ~30k tokens.

kai: that implicates kernel behavior. small_kernel likely avoids a path that pins page frames for prefetch. We should add a reproducible unit test that exercises kernel prefetch vs eviction.

maria: filed internal ticket INF-9876 with traces + heap dumps. attaching heap symbol lines: ```
0x7fffa1b2 kv_page_pin
0x7fffa2c4 kv_rebuild_locked
0x7fffb3d8 mistral_mqa_prefetch
```

irene: also check whether GQA vs MQA affects the rope slot count math. If slot indices overflow a debounce threshold, eviction skip may trigger.
aj: next steps: (1) perf team to add pprof samples during repro (kai + sam), (2) runtime to add a diagnostic flag to force unpin after prefetch (maria + irene), (3) add automated longseq CI with MQA and GQA variants.

maria: thanks — I'll run the pprof capture and drop the tar in the ticket. ETA EOD. @kai can you mobilize a quick kernel patch to experiment with unpin-after-prefetch? :pray:

kai: will try a prototype tonight, will post patch link. :hammer_and_wrench:

sam: if we confirm kernel pinning, we should also warn Dedicated customers about longseq MQA workloads until fixed.
maria: noted. I'll draft a short internal blurb for support. :memo:

perf-bot: scheduled compare run for INF-9876 tomorrow 03:00 UTC.
aj: great thread — keep the updates in INF-9876 and ping #eng-runtime once we have a repro-PR.
